newsitem.title: USA: White House still vetting Fed candidates - source.
newsitem.headline: White House still vetting Fed candidates - source.

text.p: The White House staff is still vetting potential candidates for the two vacancies on the Federal Reserve Board and has not made recommendations to President Bill Clinton, a government official said on Thursday.
"Until we know where these people vet out, we will not have any 'finalists,'" said the official, who asked not to be named. "They are moving toward the final stage of staff-level consideration."

The two Fed posts opened up earlier this year with the departure of Janet Yellen for the White House's Council of Economic Advisers and Lawrence Lindsey for the conservative American Enterprise Institute think tank.

On Wednesday, government sources said Edward Gramlich, dean of the School of Public Policy at the University of Michigan, was among those being considered by the Clinton administration for nomination to the Federal Reserve.
The sources on Wednesday said other candidates being considered included Douglas Harris, a former senior official at the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.
On Thursday, one official said Harris had been discussed as a candidate but said he did not have the impression Harris was "near the final stages" of consideration.
